rows: Sternal head: front of the manubrium. Clavicular head: upper surface of the medial third of the clavicle.
Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral half of the superior nuchal line.
Accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI). Branches of C2 and C3 carry its pain and position sense.
One side alone tilts the head toward its own shoulder and turns the face to the opposite side. Both sides together flex the neck.
hy: An accessory nerve lesion weakens turning of the face to the opposite side. A shortened muscle causes torticollis: the head tilts toward that side and the chin turns away from it.

rows: Back of the manubrium and the medial end of the clavicle.
Lower border of the body of the hyoid bone.
Lowers the hyoid bone after it has been raised in swallowing.
Inferior belly: upper border of the scapula beside the suprascapular notch.
Superior belly: lower border of the body of the hyoid bone. The two bellies meet at an intermediate tendon that a sling of fascia holds down to the clavicle.
Lowers and steadies the hyoid bone after it has been raised in swallowing.
Back of the manubrium, below the origin of sternohyoid.
Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
Lowers the larynx after it has been raised in swallowing.
Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
Lower border of the body and greater horn of the hyoid bone.
Fibers of C1 that travel with the hypoglossal nerve.
Lowers the hyoid bone. With the hyoid fixed, raises the larynx.
Digastric fossa on the inner side of the lower border of the mandible, near the midline.
Intermediate tendon of the digastric muscle, which a fibrous sling holds to the body and greater horn of the hyoid bone.
Nerve to mylohyoid, a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (mandibular nerve, CN V3).
With the posterior belly, raises the hyoid bone in swallowing. With the hyoid bone fixed, lowers the mandible to open the mouth.
Mastoid notch on the medial side of the mastoid process of the temporal bone.
Intermediate tendon of the digastric muscle, which a fibrous sling holds to the body and greater horn of the hyoid bone.
Digastric branch of the facial nerve (CN VII).
With the anterior belly, raises the hyoid bone in swallowing. With the hyoid bone fixed, helps lower the mandible.
hy: The two bellies have different nerves because they come from different pharyngeal arches: the anterior belly from the first (CN V3) and the posterior belly from the second (CN VII).

rows: A median raphe running from the mandible to the hyoid, and the body of the hyoid bone.
Nerve to mylohyoid, a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (V3).
The two muscles form the floor of the mouth. They raise the floor of the mouth, the hyoid, and the tongue in swallowing and speaking.
Styloid process of the temporal bone.
Body of the hyoid bone where it meets the greater horn. Its tendon splits around the intermediate tendon of digastric.
Raises the hyoid bone and draws it back in swallowing.
Front of the neck at the level of C3, between the mandible and the larynx. It is U-shaped.
No other bone. It is held in place by muscles and ligaments, with the thyrohyoid membrane joining it to the larynx.
Body with greater and lesser horns. It anchors the tongue and the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles.
hy: A fractured hyoid in an adult is associated with strangulation, but it is not proof of it by itself.

rows: Lower jaw. It is the only freely movable bone of the skull.
Temporal bones, at the two temporomandibular joints.
Body, angle, and ramus. Coronoid and condylar processes. The mandibular foramen, where the inferior alveolar nerve enters, and the mental foramen.
Largest cartilage of the larynx, at the level of C4 to C5. Its two plates meet in front at the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
Shields the front of the larynx. The vocal ligaments attach to the back of the angle between its plates, and its inferior horns hinge on the cricoid cartilage.
Runs from the cricoid cartilage at C6 to its division into the two main bronchi at the level of the sternal angle. The esophagus lies behind it.
Carries air to and from the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage hold it open, and the gap at the back is closed by the trachealis muscle.
hy: In the most common form of tracheoesophageal fistula, the upper esophagus ends blindly and the lower esophagus opens into the trachea. The newborn drools, chokes, and turns blue with the first feed.

rows: Front of the neck. Its two lobes lie beside the larynx and trachea and are joined by an isthmus across the 2nd to 4th tracheal rings.
Its follicular cells make the thyroid hormones T3 and T4, which set the metabolic rate. Its parafollicular (C) cells make calcitonin.
Superior thyroid artery, from the external carotid artery, and inferior thyroid artery, from the thyrocervical trunk.
hy: It forms at the back of the tongue (foramen cecum) and descends along the thyroglossal duct. A thyroglossal duct cyst is a midline neck lump that moves up when the tongue is stuck out.
Thyroid surgery puts the recurrent laryngeal nerves (hoarseness) and the parathyroid glands (low blood calcium) at risk.

rows: S-shaped bone that lies horizontally at the root of the neck and connects the upper limb to the trunk.
Manubrium of the sternum at its medial end and the acromion of the scapula at its lateral end.
The medial two-thirds are convex forward and the lateral third is flattened. Conoid tubercle and trapezoid line for the coracoclavicular ligament.
hy: One of the most often fractured bones, usually in its middle third. Its weakest point is where the middle and lateral thirds meet. Sternocleidomastoid pulls the medial piece up and the weight of the arm drags the lateral piece down.

rows: Upper part of the sternum, at the level of the T3 and T4 vertebrae.
Both clavicles, the first costal cartilages, the upper half of the second costal cartilages, and the body of the sternum.
Jugular (suprasternal) notch on its upper border, with a clavicular notch on each side.
hy: It meets the body at the sternal angle (angle of Louis), which marks the second costal cartilage and lies at the level of the disc between T4 and T5. At this level the arch of the aorta begins and ends and the trachea divides.
